verses.text: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
There he met a Jew named Aquila, who was born in Pontus. He had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to see them,
and because he made tents for a living just as they did, he stayed and worked with them.
Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks.
When Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, Paul gave all his time to preaching. He told the Jews clearly that Jesus was the Christ.

But when they turned against Paul and insulted him, he shook the dust from his clothes and said to them, "If you are lost, it is your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."
Then Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titius Justus, a man who worshipped God.
Crispus, the leader of the synagogue, and everyone in his house believed in the Lord. Many of the people in Corinth who heard Paul also believed and were baptised.
One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: "Do not be afraid. Keep on speaking, and do not be silent.
I am with you, and no one is going to attack you or harm you, because I have many people in this city."
So Paul stayed there for a year and a half, teaching them God's word.
While Gallio was governor of Achaia, the Jews got together and attacked Paul. They brought him to the court.
They said, "This man is persuading people to worship God in ways that are against the law."
Paul was about to speak, but Gallio said to the Jews, "If you were complaining about some crime or serious wrong, it would be right for me to listen to you Jews.
But since this is about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I will not be a judge of such things."
And he sent them out of the court.
Then the crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the leader of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the court. But Gallio did not care at all.

Paul stayed on in Corinth for some time. Then he said goodbye to the believers and sailed for Syria, with Priscilla and Aquila. Before he sailed, he had his hair cut off at Cenchrea because of a promise he had made to God.
They arrived at Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
They asked him to stay longer, but he said no.
As he left, he promised, "I will come back if it is God's will." Then he sailed from Ephesus.
When he landed at Caesarea, he went up to Jerusalem and greeted the church. Then he went down to Antioch.
After spending some time in Antioch, Paul left and travelled from place to place through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, making all the followers stronger.
Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, who was born in Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was a good speaker and knew the Scriptures very well.
He had been taught the way of the Lord, and he spoke with great excitement. He taught correctly about Jesus, though he knew only about John's baptism.
He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they invited him to their home and explained the way of God to him more clearly.

When Apollos wanted to go to Achaia, the believers encouraged him. They wrote to the followers there, asking them to welcome him. When he arrived, he was a great help to those who by God's grace had believed.
He strongly proved the Jews wrong in public debate, showing from the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.
